title: Composition of derived pro-etale module pullbacks
statement:
Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be morphisms of schemes, with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse images $h^{-1},k^{-1},(kh)^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R_V,R_W,R_Z$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $V_{\mathrm{proet}},W_{\mathrm{proet}},Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with identifications $k^{-1}R_V\cong R_W$ and $h^{-1}R_W\cong R_Z$, and give $(kh)^{-1}R_V$ the identification with $R_Z$ obtained through the canonical isomorphism $(kh)^{-1}\cong h^{-1}k^{-1}$. With the derived module pullbacks $Lh^*,Lk^*,L(kh)^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] there is a canonical isomorphism of functors

$$
 c_{h,k}:L(k\circ h)^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lh^*\circ Lk^*:\ D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R_V)\longrightarrow D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},R_Z),
$$

which on a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $R_V$-modules with flat terms is the class of the termwise canonical isomorphism of module pullbacks $(kh)^*\mathcal K^\bullet\cong h^*k^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ (here $k^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ is again K-flat with flat terms, so it computes $Lk^*$ and $h^*k^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ computes $Lh^*Lk^*$).

source.place: Lemma 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), for morphisms of ringed topoi; specialized to the ringed pro-etale topoi of schemes

proof.text: First construct the ordinary module comparison. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], each module pullback is left adjoint to its module direct image. On a pro-etale object T over V the direct images of an R_Z-module M have values M(Z×_V T) and M(Z×_W(W×_V T)). The canonical fibre-product isomorphism sends (z,(w,t)) to (z,t), and its inverse inserts h(z); the maps commute with arrows of T. The compatible coefficient identifications in the hypothesis give the same R_V action on these sections, since their structure maps are the adjuncts of the same composite coefficient map. Thus there is a natural module-direct-image isomorphism (kh)_*≅k_*h_*. Form the composite module adjunction using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to obtain the canonical natural module isomorphism a:(kh)^*≅h^*k^*. This is the ordinary module pullback comparison: its adjunct carries the single pullback unit to the two successive units. Write c_h:h^{-1}R_W→R_Z for the given coefficient identification. In the inverse-image/tensor presentations it sends m⊗r to (m⊗1)⊗r, and the inverse sends (m⊗s)⊗r to m⊗c_h(h^{-1}s)r, after the canonical inverse-image identification. The inverse after the forward map sends m⊗r to m⊗r because c_h(1)=1. The forward after the inverse sends (m⊗s)⊗r to (m⊗1)⊗c_h(h^{-1}s)r=(m⊗s)⊗r by balancing over h^{-1}R_W. Both maps are balanced over the other coefficient ring because the composite coefficient map is c_h composed with h^{-1}c_k under the inverse-image identification. They commute with restrictions and module maps; these calculations identify the adjunction comparison with the stated canonical termwise map.

source.place: Lemma 0D6D final identity; Modules on Sites Lemma 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules)

proof.text: In the identified-coefficient case of the item, all three module pullbacks are exact and their derived functors are induced by applying them termwise, as explicitly specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Their termwise functors therefore invert quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) to the natural isomorphism a of step 1, composed with localization to D(R_Z). It descends to a unique natural isomorphism c_{h,k}:L(kh)^*≅Lh^*Lk^*. The endpoint identifications are those of the derived operations: the latter composite applied to a complex is the class of h^*k^* of that complex. This establishes naturality on all derived morphisms, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, rather than merely on chosen resolutions.

source.place: Lemma 0D6D; derived functor construction of Lemma 06YY

proof.text: For any complex representing an input derived object choose a quasi-isomorphism P→K from a K-flat complex with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], applied to the small site V_proet and the commutative ring sheaf R_V. The computation clause of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies Lk^*K with k^*P and L(kh)^*K with (kh)^*P. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] to k, using its specified ring isomorphism as the ring map: k^*P is K-flat with flat terms over R_W. Hence it also computes Lh^*Lk^*K. The component of the descended comparison from step 2, under these identifications, is exactly the class of the termwise comparison (kh)^*P≅h^*k^*P. For an input already K-flat with flat terms take the identity resolution; this gives precisely the normalization asserted in the item. No boundedness, properness, or flatness of a scheme morphism has been used.
